openings.claim: Seat each rod against plywood corner datums and an axial stop before hand-operated M5 pressure members restrain it. Cord tethers movable members and nuts; elastic loops retain components. Deliberate seating replaces dependence on tight enclosing clearance.
openings.discriminator: Against tighter enclosing contact that may trap incomplete insertion, datum-first seating predicts lower unloaded return error; tightening may improve loaded stability alone. Equal seating with similar return defeats this explanation. The 18 mm rod may expose centerline or pointer-offset dependence despite repeatable face seating.
openings.probe: Use one reversible fixture within six plywood pieces and supplied hardware/tools; compare corner/stop versus optional enclosing contact. Verify no drilling, adhesive or permanent rod marks, captive components, hand-only adjustment/access and 90 mm cube envelope. Fabricate within 100 minutes. Per configuration: five exchanges of each original rod, then two 18 mm substitutions; log duration and unloaded error. Four ten-second 10 N trials cover initial assembly, fifth exchange of each original rod and final substitution; record target escape. Require return within 2 mm and exchanges under forty seconds. Twenty-minute testing leaves only 160 seconds for switching/setup/logging at forty-second exchanges; infeasible timing makes comparison unresolved.
openings.uncertainty: Rod orientation and pointer attachment permitting fixed face datums are unspecified. Adequate stiffness, fastening geometry and captive retention within supplied resources require verification. Defeats: inconsistent stop contact, plywood crushing, slip, angular error beyond 2 mm, substitution offset, falling parts or slow exchanges. Two reversal trials establish no cause.

lineage.reason: Preserves seating-versus-restraint mechanism, rival, substitution sensitivity and feasibility gates.

decision: Retain D1 as an unproven construction candidate. Resolve geometry, captivity and timing before comparison; complete loaded-return performance remains unproven.
